body:
actually I take this back a bit.

```
In [15]: df.groupby(level=['first', 'second']).size()
Out[15]: 
first  second
foo    two       2
dtype: int64
```

This is explicit, while specifying the names *should* be interpreted the same, I guess its not. This feature was introduced in 0.20.1.

I did some digging  and found that the bug is not related to the non unique multi-index, it rather happens with all dataframes with an equal amount of rows as levels of multi-index (and the grouper not specified as level).
Digging into the code i found that for special cases in groupby.py in line 2640 the keys for the grouping are casted to a tuplesafe array (not really sure what that is) and put into a list as the sole element. Because of that the keys are not enumerated and in_axis is set to false in line 2695 (which should be true i guess).

Removing the outer list in line 2640 fixes the here raised problem but i don't know if it is there for a good reason.

Hope that helps.
well if u can send a PR that adds your example as a test and make your change and see what fails would be great

I think i found a solution which doesn't crash the groupby tests, but i stil have to run the full test suit and integrate my own test. Hope that i can make a PR tomorrow or the day after.

Thanks for the great work you're putting into pandas!
